text: Study Sources 1 to 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘New technology will improve access to education.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘Children who use technology for education get better exam results.’
How could you test this claim? You may consider the types of information, sources of evidence
or methods you might use.

text: Study Source 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify one prediction from Ajay’s statement. Explain why this is a prediction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Salena is arguing that learning in school is better than learning from home.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Identify one opinion from Salena’s statement.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Explain how well this opinion supports Salena’s statement.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Ajay’s or Salena’s?
Your answer should consider both arguments and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different kinds of information used.

text: Study Source 4.
A government wants to improve access to education in their country.
The following actions are being considered:
• Build more schools.
• Improve transport to make it easier for children to get to school.
• Invest in technology to support remote learning.
Which one of these actions would you recommend to the government, and why?
In your answer, you should:
• state your recommendation
• give reasons and evidence to support your choice
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
• consider different arguments and perspectives.
